checks: The signed coordinate inequalities are exactly the sup-norm radius inequalities. They are simultaneously strict at z=0 and a positive continuous point of coordinate sum below a. Positivity throughout the base cube makes all 3ⁿ integer fibers exact and positive.
The sup norm gives global concavity and the stated evenness, sign and permutation symmetries. The unique central radius is 1 and every noncentral integer radius is a.

Enumerating the three sample cubes and applying positive-part powers independently gives deficits 148/2187, 28/243 and 5/64. The relevant threshold 1/3 lies in the stated range, as does the last threshold 1/2.

At a=c>0 the third comparison reduces after cancellation to 1+(3ⁿ−1)cᵈ≤2ⁿ. For fixed c,d, the left side divided by 2ⁿ tends to infinity. The source sections §§1–3 give the same construction and bounds.

overlap.comparison: The accepted positive-remainder truncation bound assumes one consecutive sequence and p≥2. The new d=2 counterexamples concern a multivariate complete cube and do not violate the accepted one-variable hypothesis.
The accepted symmetric three-site obstruction uses power one in a single integer dimension. It does not imply the d=2 multivariate failures or the stated eventual failure for 2⁻ⁿ contraction.

readability: A(c) is an unnormalized sum of radius powers. A common simplex-volume factor would cancel in each comparison.
